summary: GVE Level 3 defines the normative implementation-architecture layer that refines accepted Levels 0 through 2 without replacing or weakening them. The Level 3 root establishes implementation-facing, application-independent responsibility boundaries for the maintained core, plugins, actions, registries, validated operation contracts, workflow planning and lifecycle, evidence, operation results, and authoritative execution-record and versioned workflow-result realization. It defines the exact Level 3 specification-set decomposition while leaving detailed semantics to separately governed subordinate documents. Acceptance of Level 3 specifications does not itself accept maintained runtime code, plugin implementations, production payload schemas, or plugin-specific service behavior.

definitions.text: The application-independent normative architecture that assigns implementation-facing responsibilities for realizing accepted GVE workflow, operation, plugin, contract, planning, lifecycle, evidence, effect-state, and authoritative-result semantics without defining maintained implementation code.
The complete normative Level 3 authority consisting of exactly the root GVE-LEVEL-3 and four subordinate documents with distinct, non-overlapping primary semantic responsibilities.

The sole normative root document GVE-LEVEL-3. It establishes Level 3 identity, Level 2 parentage, inherited invariants, implementation-architecture scope, exact document decomposition, responsibility ownership, and exclusions.

The subordinate Level 3 specification GVE-LEVEL-3-RUNTIME-OWNERSHIP, which owns runtime component boundaries and core, plugin, action, registry, planning, execution-context, and shared-facility responsibility allocation.

The subordinate Level 3 specification GVE-LEVEL-3-PLUGIN-ACTION-CONTRACTS, which owns common plugin and action contracts, registration, registry validation and sealing, declared input contracts, plugin-owned interpretation, and fresh validated-operation-contract production.

The subordinate Level 3 specification GVE-LEVEL-3-WORKFLOW-PLANNING-LIFECYCLE, which owns workflow resolution, complete immutable plan acceptance, operation eligibility, dependency and actual-handoff enforcement, attempt ordering, blocking, skipping, failure, cancellation, timeout, and lifecycle realization.

The subordinate Level 3 specification GVE-LEVEL-3-EVIDENCE-RESULT-REALIZATION, which owns evidence capture and attribution, authoritative execution-record realization, operation-result production, incomplete and conflicting evidence, uncertainty, fail-closed workflow-result finalization, immutable result versions, explicit supersession, and one current lineage head.

requirements.text: Level 3 must refine implementation-facing realization of accepted Levels 0 through 2 and must not replace, weaken, collapse, contradict, bypass, or redefine any applicable workflow, operation, authority, plugin-assignment, validated-operation-contract, workflow-plan, dependency, sequencing, handoff, lifecycle, evidence, fail-closed, effect-state, or authoritative-result semantic.

The Level 3 specification set must contain exactly one root document with identity GVE-LEVEL-3, numeric level 3, normative status, parent GVE-LEVEL-2, document role root, specification-set root GVE-LEVEL-3, and no imports.
The Level 3 root must preserve the complete applicable Level 2 authority through parentage and inherited specification semantics without importing subordinate documents.

The normative Level 3 specification set must consist exactly of GVE-LEVEL-3, GVE-LEVEL-3-RUNTIME-OWNERSHIP, GVE-LEVEL-3-PLUGIN-ACTION-CONTRACTS, GVE-LEVEL-3-WORKFLOW-PLANNING-LIFECYCLE, and GVE-LEVEL-3-EVIDENCE-RESULT-REALIZATION.

Each Level 3 subordinate document must own exactly one primary semantic responsibility assigned by this root. Responsibilities must not overlap, create precedence, or permit one subordinate to redefine another; ambiguity or conflict must fail closed until corrected through separately governed specification work.

Level 3 must preserve one governed workflow containing one or more governed operations, stable workflow and operation identities, exactly one selected plugin per operation, exactly one fresh valid uniquely attributable validated operation contract per accepted operation, and complete fail-closed workflow-plan acceptance before any operation attempt.

The maintained core architecture must own only application-independent orchestration and common structural conformance, while the selected plugin and action must own application-specific action identity, input meaning, semantic interpretation, governed execution behavior, evidence obligations, and result obligations.

Level 3 must preserve explicit dependency and sequencing declarations, distinguish handoff declarations from actual runtime handoffs, preserve blocked, skipped, failed, and otherwise unattempted outcomes, and prohibit operation attempts before complete workflow-plan acceptance.

Level 3 must preserve separate requested, authorized, attempted, completed, observed, and verified claims; require traceability from every record and result claim to the governing workflow, execution, operation, plugin, action, validated contract, authority, and evidence; produce one authoritative workflow execution record for every governed workflow processing or execution identity; and permit a finalized workflow result only through fail-closed versioned result realization.

Missing, malformed, conflicting, ambiguous, stale, unauthorized, incomplete, duplicate, or non-uniquely attributable plugin, action, registry, contract, plan, dependency, handoff, evidence, effect, operation-result, or workflow-result facts must fail closed or remain explicitly incomplete or uncertain rather than being inferred as successful.

Acceptance of Level 3 specification authority does not itself accept maintained runtime implementation, language-specific interface syntax, package-manager or deployment choices, performance, caching, concurrency, production payload schemas, exhaustive action catalogs, plugin-specific filesystem, command, local-Git, remote-service, credential, publication semantics, or bootstrap executor formats.

The sole normative Level 3 root identity, status, Level 2 parentage, and no imports
Core, plugin, action, registry, contract, planning, lifecycle, evidence, and result responsibility boundaries

Complete fail-closed workflow-plan acceptance before operation attempts
Inherited dependency, handoff, effect-state, evidence, uncertainty, authoritative execution-record, finalized-result, and supersession constraints

Detailed workflow planning, operation eligibility, dependency, handoff, and lifecycle requirements assigned to GVE-LEVEL-3-WORKFLOW-PLANNING-LIFECYCLE
Detailed evidence, operation-result, uncertainty, traceability, and workflow-result requirements assigned to GVE-LEVEL-3-EVIDENCE-RESULT-REALIZATION
